rituals.name: Sunlight Exposure
rituals.description: Get 10-15 minutes of direct sunlight within an hour of waking.
rituals.science_reference: Viewing morning sunlight triggers cortisol release and sets the circadian clock.

rituals.name: Screen Light Ramp
rituals.description: Gradually increase screen brightness or use warmer light settings to ease your eyes into the day.
rituals.science_reference: Reducing blue light intensity early on prevents over-stimulation of the melanopsin ganglion cells.

rituals.name: Warm Sunlight
rituals.description: Step outside to feel the physical warmth of the sun on your skin for a few minutes.
rituals.science_reference: Infrared light and warmth promote vasodilation and stimulate mitochondrial health.

rituals.name: Calm Sigh
rituals.description: Take a deep inhale followed by a second short inhale, then exhale slowly through the mouth.
rituals.science_reference: The physiological sigh offloads maximum CO2 and rapidly lowers heart rate via the vagus nerve.

rituals.name: Box Breathing
rituals.description: Inhale, hold, exhale, and hold for 4 seconds each.
rituals.science_reference: Regulates the autonomic nervous system and lowers morning anxiety.

rituals.name: Extended Exhale Breathing
rituals.description: Practice breathing where your exhale is twice as long as your inhale to trigger relaxation.
rituals.science_reference: Longer exhales stimulate the parasympathetic nervous system to signal safety to the brain.

rituals.name: Stability Pause
rituals.description: Stand perfectly still for 60 seconds, focusing entirely on your center of gravity and balance.
rituals.science_reference: Static balance tasks increase activity in the cerebellum and improve proprioceptive awareness.

rituals.name: Stand Posture
rituals.description: Align your spine, pull your shoulders back, and stand tall to reset your physical presence.
rituals.science_reference: Upright posture is linked to lower cortisol levels and higher subjective feelings of confidence.

rituals.name: Short Walk
rituals.description: Take a 5-10 minute walk to stimulate blood flow and provide optic flow to the brain.
rituals.science_reference: Forward motion and optic flow reduce activity in the amygdala, lowering stress levels.

rituals.name: Nech Mobility
rituals.description: Perform gentle neck rolls and side-to-side stretches to release overnight tension.
rituals.science_reference: Mobilizing the cervical spine improves blood flow to the brain and reduces tension headaches.

rituals.name: Balance Hold
rituals.description: Practice standing on one leg for 30 seconds per side to engage your core and stabilizer muscles.
rituals.science_reference: Unilateral balance training strengthens the mind-body connection and core stability.

rituals.name: Reaction - Time Tap Test
rituals.description: Test your alertness by rapidly tapping a surface or using a reaction app for 30 seconds.
rituals.science_reference: Speed-based motor tasks measure and improve central nervous system firing rates.

rituals.name: Pattern
rituals.description: Identify a recurring pattern in your schedule or environment to prime your brain for logic.
rituals.science_reference: Pattern recognition exercises engage the prefrontal cortex and enhance analytical thinking.

rituals.name: Working Memory
rituals.description: Recall a list of 5-7 items or a specific sequence of events from yesterday without checking notes.
rituals.science_reference: Active recall strengthens neural pathways and improves short-term information retention.

rituals.name: Focus Caliberation
rituals.description: Stare at a single point on the wall for 60 seconds to train visual and mental focus.
rituals.science_reference: Fixed gaze (trataka) increases neuroplasticity in the circuits responsible for concentration.

rituals.name: One line intention
rituals.description: Write down a single, clear sentence defining your primary goal for the day.
rituals.science_reference: Goal setting increases dopamine synthesis by providing a clear target for the reward system.

rituals.name: Top - prioroty identification
rituals.description: Determine the one task that, if completed, would make the rest of the day feel successful.
rituals.science_reference: Identifying a 'lead domino' reduces decision fatigue and focuses cognitive resources.

rituals.name: First Task
rituals.description: Commit to starting your most important task immediately without checking emails or social media.
rituals.science_reference: Tackling the hardest task first leverages peak morning willpower and executive function.

rituals.name: gratitude acknowledgement
rituals.description: Mentally acknowledge or write down one specific thing you are genuinely thankful for today.
rituals.science_reference: Gratitude practices modulate the hypothalamus and increase serotonin production.

rituals.name: Hydration
rituals.description: Drink 500ml of water, ideally with electrolytes or a pinch of salt, to rehydrate after sleep.
rituals.science_reference: Proper hydration is essential for synaptic plasticity and maintaining cellular volume in the brain.

rituals.name: Stillness Check
rituals.description: Sit quietly while consuming your first drink or meal to practice mindful consumption.
rituals.science_reference: Eating in a state of stillness improves digestion via the cephalic phase of gastric secretion.

rituals.name: Temperature Awareness
rituals.description: Notice the temperature of your food or drink and how it affects your internal body heat.
rituals.science_reference: Sensory focus on temperature improves interoception, the body's ability to sense its internal state.
